$comment: S3 (concurrency-scaling-plan-2026-08-22.md 3.2/4, S3 row) + ER11: the queue-split vocabulary every side of the split references. 'scan_queue' and 'default_queue' are the two Celery queue names; 'scan_task_names' is every task Celery routes onto scan_queue (everything else falls through to default_queue via Celery's task_default_queue, so it is not enumerated here). default_queue is deliberately the SAME string the single-queue deployment already used as task_default_queue, so a message sitting in it from before the split is drained without a rename step. 'worker_subscriptions' is which queues each worker kind subscribes to with -Q. It replaced a single 'transition_subscribe_both_queues' boolean, which could only say 'both kinds take both queues' or 'each takes its own' and so could not express the state that is actually correct now: worker-default takes only default_queue, because a worker-default subscribed to scan_queue can pick up an hour-long scan and the short tasks it exists to serve then queue behind it (ER11); worker-scan keeps both, because it is the kind that can actually run a scan task and so remains able to drain a pre-split scan message still sitting on default_queue in a deployment upgrading late. Backend: apps/backend/tasks/celery_app.py's task_routes must route every name in scan_task_names to scan_queue and leave task_default_queue equal to default_queue. Infra: charts/trustedoss/values.yaml's worker.queues/worker.subscriptions and docker-compose.yml's worker-scan/worker-default -Q defaults must equal these values. Each side asserts against this file rather than against each other directly, per the repository's hardening rule 2 (shared vocabulary needs a cross-check, not independent copies).
